gestern.et: From Middle High German gestern, from Old High German gesteron, gesteren, from Proto-West Germanic *gesteran. Cognate with English yester, Dutch gisteren.

s: Das neue Gebäude nimmt langsam Gestalt an.
The new building is starting to take shape.
shape, build of a person, silhouette, profile
Im Licht der Laterne wurde eine bucklige Gestalt sichtbar.
The hunchbacked shape of a person became visible in the street light.
Der Bahnhofsvorplatz war von finsteren Gestalten bevölkert.
The station forecourt was populated by somber characters.
Auf dem Bahnhof dann, in dem sich senkenden Nebel, ein Gewühl von Pferden und grauen Gestalten, das zuerst unentwirrbar schien und sich dann doch rasch ordnete.
On the station then, in the sinking fog, a crowd of horses and gray characters that initially looked inextricable, but then put itself in order swiftly after all.
Gestalt.et: From Middle High German gestalt, the past participle of stellen (modern stellen, gestellt) used substantively. Cognates include Bavarian Gstoit and Yiddish געשטאַלט (geshtalt).

Gestapo.et: Contraction of Geheime Staatspolizei (“secret state police”). The predominant pronunciation with /st/ is from reading out the form as one word and thus to some extent a spelling pronunciation.

s: to confess, to admit (to a mistake, misdeed, something embarrassing); to make known
I confess my love to you.
Mein Mann hat gestanden, dass er eine Affäre hatte.
My husband admitted he had an affair.

s: Die gefällige Wohnung in einem ruhigen Bergstädtchen zieht uns an, und wir fassen den Entschluß, den ganzen Tag hier zuzubringen. Da mag denn vor allen Dingen von gestrigen Ereignissen die Rede sein.
The charming flat in a quiet mountain village attracts us, and we decide to spend the whole day here. Yesterday's events are the primary topic of conversation.
Hühner laufen umher, spindeldürre Hunde schnüffeln neugierig herum. Neben einer Schubkarre liegen die Melonen der gestrigen Ernte.
Chickens are running loose, and skinny dogs are sniffing around curiously. The harvested melons from yesterday have been placed next to a wheelbarrow.
Gestrig, aber geil [title, BMW M2 Coupe review]
gestrig.et: From Middle High German gesteric, from Old High German gesterīg. By surface analysis, gestern + -ig.

Gestade.et: From Middle High German gestade, gestat, from Old High German stad, stado, from Proto-Germanic *staþaz. Cognate with English stathe and Bavarian Gstättn (see also Gstätten).

s: Er ist nicht exzentrisch, sondern gestört.
confession (open admittance of having done something)
Die Zeitung ist auf ein gestelltes Video reingefallen.
The newspaper fell for a staged video.
rock, mass of stone, especially as part of the crust of the earth
Viele Gewässer sind mit Quecksilber belastet, das die Goldsucher einsetzen, um das Metall vom Gestein zu lösen.
Many waters are polluted with mercury, which is used by gold diggers to separate the metal from the rock.
Gestein.et:
From Middle High German gesteine, from Old High German gisteini, a collective formation equivalent to ge- + Stein.
Compare Dutch gesteente.

Gestirn.et: From Middle High German gestirn, gestirne, from Old High German gistirni. By surface analysis, ge- (collective prefix) + Stern (“star”).

s: Inmitten grün’ und klaren, seichten Wogen, / Unter wiegend’ Seegras, im Gesträuch tief verborgen, / Wo lehmig’ Kies zum Grund des Sees niedergeht, / Des im Wasser Herrschend’ Reich besteht.

Amidst green and clear, shallow waves, / Under swaying seaweed, deeply hidden in the shrubbery, / Where loamy gravel sinks down to the ground of the lake, / There is the realm of him who rules in the water.
Gesträuch.et: From Middle High German gestriuche. By surface analysis, ge- + Strauch.

s: Wenn hier geraucht wird, dann genussvoll, nicht gestresst. Bourgeois liegt die Zigarette zwischen Zeige- und Mittelfinger, vielleicht ist Catherine Deneuve-mäßig der Arm angewinkelt.

Gestrüpp.et: Derived from ge- + Middle High German struppe.

gestiefelt.et: From ge- + Stiefel + -t or past participle of stiefeln.

gestielt.et: From ge- + Stiel + -t or past participle of stielen.

geständig.et:
From Middle High German gestendec.
See also Geständnis.

Gest.et: Low German, from Middle Low German gest, from Old Saxon *gest, from, from Proto-West Germanic *jestu. Compare Dutch gist, English yeast, Swedish jäst, Icelandic jöstur.

s: agent noun of gestalten: one who forms, shapes, creates or arranges something
Gestalter.et: gestalten (“to form, to shape, to arrange”) + -er

s: nominalization of gestaltetes: something formed, shaped, designed or arranged
Es gab dort sehr viel neu Gestaltetes zu sehen.
Gestaltetes.et: Nominalization of gestaltet (“formed, shaped, designed, arranged”).

s: skinwalker (male or of unspecified gender) (in Navajo folklore)
last night; during the night preceding the present day
Gestern Nacht hatte ich stundenlang wachgelegen, aber heute Nacht konnte ich sehr gut schlafen.
The night before last night I had lain awake for hours, but last night I slept very well.

Gestüpp.et: From Middle High German stuppe, stüppe, from Old High German stuppi, from Proto-West Germanic *stubbju, from Proto-Germanic *stubjuz (“dust”).

s: gestures (as a motion of the limbs or body, especially one made to emphasize speech)
Gestik.et: Borrowed from Latin gesticulus, diminutive of gestus.

s: Die meisten begannen Briefe mit den denkbar gestelztesten, linkischsten und ungeschicktesten Wendungen.
bungle, botching, hack job, half measure

Gestalt psychology (school of psychology that emerged in the early twentieth century in Austria and Germany as a theory of perception, that was a rejection of basic principles of Wilhelm Wundt's and Edward Titchener's elementalist and structuralist psychology)
Gestalt therapy (existential and experiential psychotherapy that focuses on the individual's experience in the present moment)
